subject: Meteorology
title: How Lightning Forms
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on How Lightning Forms.

hook.text: Lightning is a massive electrical discharge—a spark jumping across a gap of kilometers inside a storm cloud.

buildup.text: Collisions between ice crystals and graupel inside the cloud separate charges—positive up, negative below.

discovery.text: When the electric field grows strong enough, a stepped leader zig-zags downward—seeking a path to the ground.

twist.text: An upward streamer rises from the surface to meet it—the connection completes the circuit in a brilliant flash.

climax.text: The return stroke heats the channel to 30,000°C—five times hotter than the Sun's surface—in microseconds.

punchline.text: Five times the Sun's surface—packed into a channel as wide as a thumb.

quiz.question: How hot is a lightning channel?
